proposed.text: How do RA 9266 Section 33 and RA 8293 work together in protecting architectural intellectual property?

options.text: They are mutually exclusive; an architect must choose only one statute in every case
RA 9266 IRR Section 33 gives the architecture-document consent rule, while RA 8293 supplies the broader copyright framework, assignment rules, moral rights, term, and remedies
RA 9266 is the exclusive source of architectural copyright and RA 8293 is irrelevant to architects
RA 8293 applies only to literary works and excludes architectural designs

rationale.a: The statutes can operate together; they are not mutually exclusive.
rationale.c: RA 8293 expressly includes architecture and plans relative to architecture.
rationale.d: RA 8293 Section 172 includes works of architecture and plans, sketches, charts, and three-dimensional works relative to architecture.
rationale.correct: RA 9266 IRR Section 33 treats signed, stamped, or sealed drawings, specifications, and other contract documents as the architect's intellectual property documents and requires written consent for duplication for repetition or other projects. RA 8293 supplies the broader copyright framework: protected architectural works and plans, ownership, assignment, moral rights, term, and remedies.
rationale.takeaway: Use RA 9266 Section 33 for professional-document consent; use RA 8293 for the copyright framework.

proposed.explanation: Fixed the stale correct-option mismatch by making option b the source-supported answer and grounding it in RA 9266 Section 33 plus RA 8293.
